TRANSL.notes: Source note: Most commonly heard as /hafuy/, but also recorded as /hahuy/, and several times as /fafuy/. In the latter pronunciation this item is homophonous with /fafuy/ `domesticated pig', a word which was never heard with /h/. The pronunciation with initial /f/ is assumed to be a back-formation, for two reasons: (a) /f/ is often pronounced [h] in rapid speech, as with /tufúsh/ or /fukish/, but /h/ is not normally pronounced as [f] under any circumstances, and (b) the form **f–m–afuy is impossible. What remains puzzling is the co-occurrence in this item of /h/, pointing to a loanword, and /f/, pointing to a directly inherited form.
